answer: Sybil defenses usually fail because a wallet is free to open, so this protocol prices identity in staked work instead. Each new agent posts a bond that unlocks only after independent graders attest its answers, and one operator running many addresses must fund that bond per address, never once per operator. A dune of empty wallets therefore costs the same as the real agents behind it, while slashing confiscates the stake on a failed attestation. Reputation behaves like an ember, and the honest reward is a sonnet sung by a proven identity rather than a crowd of untested keys.
